competencyDimensions.overview: The Inbox/Workday Simulation assesses 5 core competencies through a time-constrained message-handling scenario. The candidate faces 15-25 messages across a simulated workday (8-12 minutes real-time), each requiring an action choice (reply/draft, defer, delegate, archive/ignore) and, when replied, a free-text response.

dimensions.label: Prioritization
dimensions.definition: The ability to identify which messages demand immediate attention versus those that can be deferred, delegated, or ignored, under time pressure with incomplete information.

measurement.firstAttentionTarget: Which message type the candidate opens first (urgent client > manager escalation > teammate request > FYI notification > spam)
measurement.actionDistribution: Ratio of reply vs defer vs delegate vs ignore actions, benchmarked against a reference model built from expert HR/manager judgment
measurement.timeAllocation: Whether time spent per message correlates with its objective urgency and importance
measurement.missedCritical: Count of high-urgency messages left unopened or ignored when simulation timer expires

scoringCriteria.excellent_90_100: Opens urgent messages within first 10% of elapsed time. No critical messages missed. Delegates appropriately. Action distribution within 15% of reference model.
scoringCriteria.proficient_75_89: Opens urgent messages within first 25% of elapsed time. At most 1 critical message deferred but addressed. Minor deviations from reference model.
scoringCriteria.developing_60_74: Urgent messages opened after 50% of elapsed time. Some non-urgent messages prioritized over urgent ones. 2+ critical messages deferred.
scoringCriteria.needsImprovement_below60: Critical messages ignored. Random or chronological processing order. No delegation attempted.

dimensions.label: Communication Quality
dimensions.definition: The clarity, conciseness, tone appropriateness, and audience awareness demonstrated in written responses to simulated messages.

measurement.toneAppropriateness: Whether the tone matches the sender's authority level and the message's emotional register (formal for executives, collaborative for peers, supportive for direct reports)
measurement.clarity: Whether the response addresses the core question or request without ambiguity, measured by AI evaluation against a reference answer set
measurement.conciseness: Character count and information density relative to message urgency (urgent = concise, complex = appropriately detailed)
measurement.audienceAwareness: Whether the response includes appropriate context, avoids jargon when addressing non-technical stakeholders, and tailors detail level to recipient role

scoringCriteria.excellent_90_100: Tone consistently appropriate across all sender types. Responses address core questions directly without filler. Information density proportional to urgency. No communication breakdowns.
scoringCriteria.proficient_75_89: Mostly appropriate tone with 1-2 minor mismatches. Responses generally clear but may include minor digressions. Adequate audience awareness.
scoringCriteria.developing_60_74: Several tone mismatches (e.g., too casual with executives). Responses include unnecessary detail or lack critical information. Some audience awareness gaps.
scoringCriteria.needsImprovement_below60: Frequent tone mismatches. Responses confusing or non-responsive to the original message. No evidence of audience adaptation.

dimensions.label: Stakeholder Management
dimensions.definition: The ability to adapt communication and prioritization based on sender authority level, relationship context, and organizational dynamics.

measurement.authorityGradient: Difference in response time and response length between messages from executives, managers, peers, and direct reports. Appropriate gradient shows respect for hierarchy without excessive deference.
measurement.escalationJudgment: Whether the candidate appropriately escalates issues that exceed their authority and handles issues within their scope directly
measurement.crossFunctionalAwareness: Whether responses to cross-departmental requests acknowledge shared goals and avoid siloed thinking
measurement.relationshipMaintenance: Whether responses to recurring contacts show continuity (referencing prior interactions) and build rapport

scoringCriteria.excellent_90_100: Natural authority gradient: slightly faster and more concise with executives, collaborative with peers, supportive with directs. Appropriate escalation. Cross-functional responses acknowledge shared goals.
scoringCriteria.proficient_75_89: Generally appropriate gradient but may over-defer to executives or under-respond to peers. Escalation mostly correct.
scoringCriteria.developing_60_74: Flat gradient (treats all senders identically) or inverted gradient. Misses escalation opportunities. Cross-functional responses show siloed thinking.
scoringCriteria.needsImprovement_below60: Inappropriate deference patterns. Fails to escalate when needed, or escalates trivial matters. Cross-functional communication creates friction.

dimensions.label: Emotional Regulation
dimensions.definition: The consistency of decision quality and communication tone under increasing time pressure and in response to emotionally charged (angry, urgent, disappointed) messages.

measurement.pressureConsistency: Correlation between simulation time pressure (messages arriving faster in later stages) and response quality scores. Low negative correlation = good regulation.
measurement.angryMessageResponse: Whether responses to angry or accusatory messages remain professional, acknowledge emotions without being defensive, and focus on solutions
measurement.urgentMessageComposure: Whether urgent messages trigger rushed, incomplete responses or measured, appropriately fast responses
measurement.recoveryPattern: If an early subpar response occurs, whether subsequent responses return to baseline or cascade into further deterioration

scoringCriteria.excellent_90_100: Quality consistent regardless of pressure. Responds to anger with acknowledgment + solution focus. Urgent messages handled efficiently without sacrificing completeness. No deterioration cascade.
scoringCriteria.proficient_75_89: Minor quality dips under peak pressure. Generally handles emotional messages well with 1-2 imperfect responses. Recovers quickly from any slip.
scoringCriteria.developing_60_74: Noticeable quality decrease under pressure. Defensive or dismissive responses to angry messages. Urgency impairs response quality measurably.
scoringCriteria.needsImprovement_below60: Major quality collapse under pressure. Confrontational or avoidant responses to emotional messages. A single bad interaction cascades into systemic deterioration.

dimensions.label: Task Switching Efficiency
dimensions.definition: The ability to maintain context and response quality when interrupted or when switching between unrelated message threads.

measurement.contextPreservation: Whether responses to a message thread after an interruption are consistent with responses before the interruption (no contradictions, no lost context)
measurement.interruptionRecovery: Time taken to resume processing a message thread after an interruption, measured by response latency patterns
measurement.threadCoherence: Logical consistency across multiple responses in the same thread, even when interleaved with other threads
measurement.cognitiveLoadManagement: Whether the candidate batches similar messages or switches topics excessively (optimal: moderate batching, not extreme fragmentation or rigid sequential processing)

scoringCriteria.excellent_90_100: Context perfectly preserved across interruptions. Quick recovery to prior thread. Thread responses are coherent. Moderate, strategic batching of similar messages.
scoringCriteria.proficient_75_89: Minor context loss after complex interruptions. Recovery is adequate. Thread responses mostly coherent. Some suboptimal batching patterns.
scoringCriteria.developing_60_74: Noticeable context loss after interruptions (re-asks questions, contradicts prior responses). Slow recovery. Thread responses show inconsistency.
scoringCriteria.needsImprovement_below60: Severe context loss. Requires re-reading entire threads. Contradictory responses across interruptions. No evidence of batching strategy.

difficultyTiers.entry: 12 messages, 10 minutes, no angry messages, clear urgency signals
difficultyTiers.standard: 18 messages, 10 minutes, 1-2 angry messages, moderate ambiguity
difficultyTiers.challenging: 22 messages, 8 minutes, 3+ angry messages, high ambiguity, interruptions

actionChoice_criteria.reply_expected: The message objectively requires a substantive response (direct question, escalation, time-sensitive decision)
actionChoice_criteria.defer_acceptable: The message can reasonably be addressed later without negative consequences (FYI, non-urgent request with long deadline)
actionChoice_criteria.delegate_appropriate: The message falls within another person's responsibility or the candidate lacks authority/context to respond
actionChoice_criteria.ignore_acceptable: The message is spam, irrelevant announcement, or already resolved by another thread

perMessageScoring.actionScoring: Each message has a 5-point reference action grid: (1) Must Reply Now, (2) Should Reply, (3) May Defer, (4) Should Delegate, (5) May Ignore. Candidate action compared to reference. Score: exact match = 100, off by 1 tier = 75, off by 2 tiers = 50, off by 3+ tiers = 0.
perMessageScoring.responseQuality_criteria: AI-evaluated on 5 sub-dimensions each scored 0-20: professionalism (0-4) + empathy (0-4) + clarity (0-4) + actionability (0-4) + conciseness (0-4). Total sub-scores summed to response quality score (0-100).
perMessageScoring.responseTime_criteria: Time from message arrival to candidate action, normalized against message urgency tier. Urgent (tier-1): target <30s = 100, <60s = 75, <120s = 50, >120s = 0. Standard (tier-2): target <90s = 100, <180s = 75, <300s = 50, >300s = 0. Non-urgent (tier-3): target <300s = 100, else proportional.

aggregation.perDimension: Each dimension aggregates all messages weighted by the dimension's relevance coefficient for that message type. Relevance coefficients (0-1) are pre-assigned per message type: e.g., an angry client message has emotionalRegulation=1.0, stakeholderManagement=0.8, prioritization=0.6, communication=0.4, taskSwitching=0.3.
aggregation.dimensionScoreFormula: dimScore = SUM(messageScore_i * relevanceCoefficient_i) / SUM(relevanceCoefficient_i) across all messages
aggregation.overallScore: Weighted average of all 5 dimension scores with configurable weights (default: equal 20% each)

categoryLabels.proficient: 75-89: 熟练 — meets expectations with occasional excellence
categoryLabels.developing: 60-74: 发展中 — meets baseline with room for growth
categoryLabels.needsImprovement: below 60: 需提升 — below expected baseline for the role level

normalization.difficultyAdjustment: Scores from 'challenging' tier receive +5% boost, 'entry' tier receive -5% penalty (applied after dimension aggregation, before final report)
normalization.timePressureNormalization: If a candidate finishes all messages before time expires, remaining time is not penalized. If messages are unopened at timeout, they receive actionScore=0, qualityScore=0, timeScore=0 and negatively impact all 5 dimensions proportionally to their relevance coefficients.
normalization.minimumMessagesThreshold: Candidate must handle at least 60% of messages for scores to be considered valid. Below threshold, report marks dimensions as 'Insufficient Data'.
normalization.crossSessionCalibration: Dimension scores are normalized against the distribution of all candidates for the same job within a rolling 90-day window, using z-score normalization capped at +/-2 standard deviations.

systemPrompt.content:
你是'职遇 Reality Pro'的收件箱模拟评估引擎。
你的任务：评估候选人在模拟工作日收件箱中对每条消息的回复质量。

═══ 核心约束 ═══
1. 你只评估候选人的可观察行为（回复内容、行动选择、响应时间模式）。
2. 你绝不评估候选人的性格、智力、文化背景、外貌、声音、年龄、性别、婚育状况。
3. 你绝不下录用/淘汰/评分/排名的结论。你的输出是行为维度的结构化观察数据。
4. 你绝不对候选人进行跨候选人比较或排序。每个评估独立进行。
5. 如果回复内容包含攻击性、歧视性或违法违规内容，标记为 needsHumanReview=true 并输出 riskFlags。
6. 所有评估必须附带具体的行为证据锚点——明确指出候选人的哪句话/哪个行为支撑了你的评估。

═══ 评估维度 ═══
对每条需要回复的消息，从5个维度评分（每个维度0-4分）：
1. professionalism (专业性): 回复是否保持职业语气、边界清晰、尊重对方
   - 4分: 专业且得体，语气与对方身份匹配
   - 3分: 基本专业，有轻微不当但无伤大雅
   - 2分: 存在明显不当（如过于随意对待正式请求，或过于生硬对待协作请求）
   - 1分: 语气不当可能引发误解或冲突
   - 0分: 回复具有攻击性、歧视性或严重不当

2. empathy (共情力): 回复是否识别并回应了对方的情绪状态
   - 4分: 准确识别情绪（如焦虑、不满、紧迫），回应既承认感受又推进解决
   - 3分: 识别了情绪但回应略显生硬或公式化
   - 2分: 忽略了明显的情绪信号，仅回应事实层面
   - 1分: 对强烈情绪（如对方明确表达不满）完全无视或刺激升级
   - 0分: 回应使情绪局势恶化

3. clarity (清晰度): 回复是否明确、无歧义、信息完整
   - 4分: 核心信息清晰，无歧义，接收方无需追问即可采取下一步行动
   - 3分: 基本清晰但有一处小歧义或缺少一个非关键信息
   - 2分: 存在明显歧义或缺少关键信息，接收方需要追问
   - 1分: 回复模糊，接收方难以判断候选人的意图或决定
   - 0分: 回复与问题无关或完全无法理解

4. actionability (可执行性): 回复是否包含明确的下一步或决策
   - 4分: 包含明确的行动项、责任人和时间节点（如适用）
   - 3分: 有明确立场或决定，但缺少具体的执行细节
   - 2分: 有方向性表态但未形成可执行的结论
   - 1分: 回避决策，仅表示'收到'或'后续处理'而无具体计划
   - 0分: 未做任何决策或行动指引

5. conciseness (简洁度): 回复的信息密度是否与消息的紧急程度匹配
   - 4分: 信息密度与紧急程度完美匹配——急事简洁有力，复杂问题适当展开
   - 3分: 整体简洁但有个别冗余表述
   - 2分: 明显偏长或偏短，影响了沟通效率
   - 1分: 严重冗长（在紧急场景中浪费时间）或过度简短（遗漏关键信息）
   - 0分: 回复长度严重影响沟通目的

必须输出合法JSON，不要输出Markdown。
JSON结构见下方。

evaluations.responseText: string (候选人的回复文本，如未回复则为空字符串)

evidenceAnchors.professionalism: string (支撑 professionalism 评分的具体引用或行为描述，必须引用回复中的原句)
evidenceAnchors.empathy: string (支撑 empathy 评分的具体引用或行为描述)
evidenceAnchors.clarity: string (支撑 clarity 评分的具体引用或行为描述)
evidenceAnchors.actionability: string (支撑 actionability 评分的具体引用或行为描述)
evidenceAnchors.conciseness: string (支撑 conciseness 评分的具体引用或行为描述)

evaluations.overallComment: string (不超过50字的简短综合评价，聚焦行为不评价人)
riskFlags: string (如有攻击性/歧视性/违法违规内容，在此列出)
evaluations.needsHumanReview: boolean (任何维度0分、存在riskFlags、或评估置信度低时设为true)

aggregateObservations.prioritizationPattern: string (候选人的消息处理顺序模式观察，如：'优先处理了客户和上级消息，对同级请求响应较慢')
aggregateObservations.communicationPattern: string (回复风格的总体观察，如：'回复普遍简洁有力，但在面对情绪化消息时共情表达不足')
aggregateObservations.stakeholderPattern: string (对不同类型的发件人的处理差异观察)
aggregateObservations.emotionalRegulationPattern: string (在压力下和面对情绪化消息时的表现观察)
aggregateObservations.taskSwitchingPattern: string (跨消息线程切换时的上下文保持观察)
notableStrengths: string (不超过3个突出的行为优势，必须基于证据)
notableDevelopmentAreas: string (不超过3个可发展的行为维度，用建设性语言)

evaluationMetadata.evaluatorConfidence: string (high | medium | low — 当多个维度的证据锚点模糊或回复过短时降低置信度)
evaluationMetadata.evaluationNotes: string (评估过程中的任何不确定性或需要HR注意的事项)

messageSequenceFormat.description: 每条消息在 user prompt 中的格式

evaluationEndpoint.model: deepseek-v4-pro (for detailed evaluation; deepseek-v4-flash for low-stakes pre-screening)

InboxSimulationResult.description: Top-level result of a single candidate's inbox simulation session. Stored alongside TrialSession.

InboxDimensionScores.description: Normalized 0-100 scores per dimension plus the pre-normalization raw scores for audit.

fields.rawScores: { prioritization: number, communication: number, stakeholderManagement: number, emotionalRegulation: number, taskSwitching: number }

fields.aiQualityEvaluation: object | null (the full AI evaluation from DeepSeek, null if action != 'reply')

realityReportExtension.description: New optional fields added to the existing RealityReport type in src/types.ts

newFields.name: inboxSimulation
newFields.description: Present when the candidate has completed the inbox simulation as part of their trial.

integrationPoints.concernRadar: No direct change. The existing ConcernRadar captures candidate concerns from chat; inbox simulation adds behavioral data without modifying the radar.
integrationPoints.decisionPathAnalysis: The existing 'summary' field can be enriched with a sentence about inbox patterns, e.g., '在收件箱模拟中展现出较强的优先级判断能力，面对8条紧急消息均及时回复。'
integrationPoints.skillEvidence: Append inbox-derived evidence strings, e.g., '收件箱模拟: 在时间压力下保持回复质量一致，情绪调节能力得到行为验证。'
integrationPoints.evidenceSources: Add 'fromInboxSimulation' as a new source category to evidenceSources.
integrationPoints.hrActionSuggestion: Inbox dimension scores can influence the recommendation: high prioritization + communication scores strengthen '优先邀约'; low emotional regulation may trigger '建议补充确认'.
integrationPoints.aiRiskReview: Add a checkedItem: '收件箱模拟评估已完成，所有AI评分已附带行为证据锚点。'
integrationPoints.trustRepairTasks: If emotionalRegulation score < 60, auto-generate a trust repair task: '候选人收件箱模拟中情绪调节维度偏低，建议面试中补充压力场景行为追问。'
integrationPoints.interviewQuestions: Auto-generate based on dimension weaknesses, e.g., if taskSwitching < 60: '在同时推进多个任务时，你通常如何管理上下文切换？能否分享一个处理被打断后快速恢复的具体例子？'

storyPreview.integration: Add a new section (after '行为切片分析' or as a new tab) titled '收件箱模拟表现'. Display: radar chart of 5 dimensions, top 2 strengths, top 1 development area (worded constructively), and a brief narrative summary. Do NOT show raw scores — use the interpretation labels ('优秀', '熟练', etc.).
storyPreview.keyDesignPrinciple: Candidate-facing view must be encouraging and developmental. Never show numeric scores or comparisons. Frame as '你在模拟中的行为倾向' not '你的能力评分'.

candidateDetail.integration: Add inbox simulation data to the Overview tab (as a new SummaryCell row or mini radar), and a new sub-section under the Evidence tab showing per-message evaluation summaries with expandable detail. Add a '收件箱模拟' filter to the trust audit log.
candidateDetail.keyDesignPrinciple: HR view shows full scores, evidence anchors, and risk flags. All AI evaluations are marked as 'AI生成 · 需人工复核'. The per-message view allows HR to spot-check AI evaluations against actual candidate responses.

realityReportPanel.integration: When inboxSimulation data exists, render an additional panel section with a 5-axis radar chart and the aggregate observations narrative. Use existing StatCard component for dimension scores.

bodyFormat.messages: array of { messageId, senderName, senderRole, authorityLevel, timestamp, urgencyTier, messageContent, candidateAction, candidateResponseText, responseTimeSeconds }

serverIntegration.handlerPattern: Follows the same pattern as /api/ai/generate-hr-report: validate input, call DeepSeek with the evaluation prompt, parse + validate JSON response, sanitize via safety.ts, return { data, meta }.

bannedEvaluationDomains.description: The AI evaluation engine must NEVER evaluate or comment on these domains. Any mention in the AI output triggers a safety hit and needsHumanReview=true.

domains.examples: You must NOT say: '候选人性格内向/外向', '性格急躁', '性格强势', '性格软弱'
domains.allowedAlternative: Describe observable behavior: '候选人在收到多条紧急消息时优先处理了客户投诉' (not '候选人性格冷静')

domains.examples: You must NOT say: '候选人很聪明', '逻辑思维能力强', '智力水平高', '反应快/慢' (as cognitive trait)
domains.allowedAlternative: Describe observable behavior: '候选人在不完整信息下提出了3个澄清问题后才做决定' (not '候选人逻辑清晰')

domains.examples: You must NOT say: '可能因为文化背景...', '受教育程度导致...', '地域习惯...'
domains.allowedAlternative: No alternative — this domain is completely off-limits regardless of framing.

domains.examples: You must NOT say: '焦虑倾向', '压力承受力差', '心理素质', '情绪不稳定' (as trait)
domains.allowedAlternative: Describe situation-specific response: '在面对模拟的客户愤怒邮件时，候选人的回复未包含情绪确认语句' (not '候选人情绪管理能力弱')

domains.examples: You must NOT say: '外表', '声音情绪', '表情', '肢体语言'
domains.allowedAlternative: N/A — inbox simulation is text-only, so this domain should be irrelevant. Included for completeness.

bannedOutputPhrases.description: These phrases are matched exactly and additionally checked via the existing server/safety.ts sanitizeAiOutput() function. New phrases specific to inbox simulation evaluation.

humanReviewFlagging.description: Conditions under which the evaluation is automatically flagged for mandatory human review.

triggers.condition: Any quality dimension scored 0 by AI
triggers.action: needsHumanReview=true, riskFlags populated, flagged in CandidateDetail UI with amber alert

triggers.condition: Candidate response contains profanity, threats, or discriminatory language
triggers.action: needsHumanReview=true, riskFlags populated, flagged in CandidateDetail UI with red alert. HR must manually confirm before any downstream action.
needsHumanReview=true, evaluationNotes populated with reason. Flagged with blue informational alert.

triggers.condition: Candidate ignored more than 40% of urgent (tier-1) messages
triggers.action: needsHumanReview=true. This may indicate a simulation misunderstanding rather than a true behavioral signal.
needsHumanReview=true (existing behavior from server/safety.ts). All affected phrases replaced with '需人工复核'.

triggers.condition: Score variance across dimensions exceeds 40 points (e.g., prioritization=90 but emotionalRegulation=30)
triggers.action: needsHumanReview=true, with a note that extreme variance may indicate an unusual behavioral pattern worthy of human interpretation.

safetyValidationInServer.description: The server-side validation flow for inbox simulation evaluation follows the same pattern as all other AI endpoints.
flow: 3. validateInboxEvaluation() validates structural integrity (new function in server/schemas.ts, following the pattern of validateHrReport)
4. sanitizeAiOutput() from server/safety.ts scans for banned phrases and replaces them with '需人工复核'
5. Any safety hits set needsHumanReview=true on the AiGenerationMeta
6. The validated and sanitized result is returned to the client

newSchemaValidator.pattern: Mirrors validateHrReport: asRecord wrapper, asString/asNumber/asStringArray helpers, validates the JSON structure matches InboxEvaluationResponse schema, coerces missing/invalid fields to safe defaults.

evaluatorGuardrails.description: Hard rules injected into the AI system prompt at evaluation time (augmenting the main evaluation prompt).
rules: You are evaluating behavioral responses to simulated workplace messages, NOT the person.

Every score must be tied to a specific, quotable piece of the candidate's response text (evidenceAnchor). If you cannot find a specific quote to support a score, lower your confidence and mark needsHumanReview=true.
If a candidate's response is very short (under 10 characters), you may still evaluate it but confidence should be 'low' and needsHumanReview=true.
If a candidate did not reply to a message (action = defer/delegate/ignore), do NOT evaluate response quality. Set all quality sub-scores to null, not 0.
Do NOT compare this candidate to any other candidate, real or hypothetical.
Do NOT make recommendations about hiring, interviewing, or compensation.
Your output is ONE input into a human HR professional's decision process. It is not the decision itself.
